ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the satellite orbital radii of the two planets are the same, the centripetal acceleration of the satellite of planet A is greater than the centripetal acceleration of the satellite of planet B
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis represents the cube of the orbital radius r^3, and the horizontal axis represents the square of the period T^2. The dashed extension lines of the two straight lines A and B both point to the origin, indicating that they can be regarded as linear relationships passing through the origin; among them, line A is steeper than line B, that is, in the r^3-T^2 graph, the slope of A is greater than the slope of B. In the figure, at T0^2, A corresponds to RA^3, and B corresponds to RB^3.
Reasoning: From Kepler's third law or from universal gravitation providing centripetal force, there is T^2 = 4π^2 r^3 / (GM), therefore the graph slope r^3/T^2 = GM / 4π^2. The greater the slope, the greater the GM of the central planet. From the figure it can be known that GM_A > GM_B. If the satellite orbital radii of the two planets are the same, the centripetal acceleration a = GM/r^2; because r is the same and GM_A > GM_B, therefore a_A > a_B.
